hints: Focus on the clue that no gas was produced, so think about which type of acid reaction makes only a salt and water.
Remember that propanoic acid with a carbonate or hydrogencarbonate always gives off carbon dioxide gas as well as the salt.
Check which reagent can neutralise the acid to give sodium propanoate plus only water, with nothing bubbling off.
walkthrough:
**Identify the acid and the salt**

Propanoic acid is $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{COOH}$ and sodium propanoate is $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{COONa}$. This is a neutralisation to make the sodium salt of the acid.

**Recall the two main routes to a salt**

With a base (alkali):
$$\text{acid + base} \rightarrow \text{salt + water}$$
With a carbonate or hydrogencarbonate:
$$\text{acid + carbonate} \rightarrow \text{salt + water + carbon dioxide}$$

**Apply the no gas clue**

The question says no gas was produced. That rules out any reaction that makes $\text{CO}_2$. Only neutralisation by a base fits:
$$\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{COOH + NaOH} \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{COONa + H}_2\text{O}$$

options.A: Acid plus hydrogencarbonate gives salt, water and carbon dioxide gas, so gas would be seen. This contradicts the no gas observation.
options.B: Sodium hydroxide neutralises propanoic acid to give sodium propanoate and water only, with no gas evolved. This matches the observation perfectly.
options.C: Acid plus carbonate gives salt, water and carbon dioxide gas, so bubbling would be seen. This contradicts the no gas observation.
options.D: Sodium sulfate is the salt of a strong acid and will not react with a weak carboxylic acid like propanoic acid. No sodium propanoate would form.
